newsitem.title: UK: UK's Redwood says he can still win Tory leadership.
newsitem.headline: UK's Redwood says he can still win Tory leadership.

text.p: Former cabinet minister John Redwood said on Wednesday he still believed he could win the race to succeed John Major as Conservative leader.
Redwood told a news conference: "Of course I want to win this election. I believe I can win this election."
Redwood came third in Tuesday's first round ballot with 27 votes, trailing former finance minister Kenneth Clarke with 49 and former Welsh Secretary William Hague who took 41.
But Redwood was dealt a blow when the fourth placed Peter Lilley and fifth placed Michael Howard quit and backed Hague.
Redwood said he hoped to pick up support from Lilley and Howard supporters despite their endorsement of Hague.

Pledging to fight the race and lead the party as a "traditional conservative", Redwood said Clarke was too left wing and Hague too unsure of what he wanted to defend Britain in Europe, which he described as the key question facing the party.
"Please realise the answer has to be never to a single currency...to the social chapter," Redwood said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
